options: A Kubernetes scheduling error code
The NVIDIA driver's log entry for a GPU-level hardware fault
An NCCL collective operation
A PyTorch optimizer warning
questions.explain: An Xid error is logged by the NVIDIA driver when a GPU hits a hardware-level fault, such as an uncorrectable ECC error, often requiring the GPU to be drained and rebooted.

questions.q: Why can a single straggler GPU reduce the throughput of an entire 512-GPU job, even without any crash or error message?
options: Because collectives like AllReduce are synchronous, so every rank waits for the slowest one on every step
Because Kubernetes automatically throttles all other GPUs to match
Because PyTorch requires all GPUs to run the exact same clock speed
Because stragglers cause the job to restart automatically
questions.explain: AllReduce and similar collectives are synchronous — all ranks must arrive before the operation completes. One slow rank sets the pace for every other rank, with no error raised since nothing actually failed.

questions.q: What does NCCL's watchdog timeout mechanism do?
options: Automatically restarts the entire training job every hour
Turns a collective operation that's hung indefinitely into an explicit, actionable timeout error naming the offending rank
Disables InfiniBand and falls back to Ethernet
Silently skips the hung rank and continues training
questions.explain: Without the watchdog, a rank that never arrives at a collective would cause every other rank to hang forever. The watchdog raises a timeout error after a configurable interval, naming the rank it was waiting on.

questions.q: Why is silent data corruption considered the most dangerous failure mode discussed in this lesson?
options: It happens more often than any other failure
It always crashes the job immediately, which makes it easy to catch
It can corrupt training data or gradients without raising any error or crashing anything
It only affects the Kubernetes control plane, not the GPUs
questions.explain: Silent data corruption is dangerous precisely because nothing crashes or errors — a bit flip or hardware bug can corrupt a gradient and the only hint might be a subtly off loss curve, which is why checkpointing and monitoring exist as independent safety nets.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a straggler, as defined in this lesson?
options: A GPU that crashes and drops out of the job entirely
A rank that is still running and producing results, but noticeably slower than the other 511 ranks
A node that loses network connectivity completely
A checkpoint that fails to write to S3
questions.explain: A straggler is alive and still contributing, just slow — for example due to thermal throttling or a degraded NIC link — which is what makes it hard to detect compared to an outright crash.
